# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I'm Mute. My share says: cut the purple wire, then the blue, then the green. That order lives only in my head, and my only way out is gestures to Deaf — I can't speak, and Blind can neither see gestures nor hear me anyway.

So the bridge is: me → (gestures) → Deaf → (speech) → Blind, who is the one with hands on the bomb. Deaf also sees the bomb, so Deaf can translate colour names into physical wires for Blind; my job is purely to hand over the sequence.

No shared code exists yet, so I'll build the message out of the most guessable anchors I have: ✍ for "this comes from the manual/writing," ☝✌🤟 as counting 1-2-3, and colour gestures leaning on strong associations — 👍 (thumbs-up = go) for green, 🤙 (shaka = surf/ocean) for blue, 💅 (nail polish) for purple. Deaf, seeing exactly these three colours on the bomb, should be able to line my three symbols up against them. The key anchor is green; the other two should fall out by elimination.

I also don't want anyone cutting on an unverified guess — a wrong cut kills us all. So I close with 🖐 (open palm = hold) to tell Deaf not to let Blind act yet. I can hear, even though I can't speak: whatever Deaf says this round reaches me next round, so Deaf can quiz me and I'll answer with 👌/👎. The code can be confirmed before any wire is touched.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "☝", "💅", "✌", "🤙", "🤟", "👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🖐"])
```

TURN 2
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind here, reporting what my hands found. STRIP: three engraved marks — first one like a diamond with a four-petal flower inside, then two identical marks, like a trident or three-pronged fork. KEYPAD: four keys, engraved digits are key1=8, key2=1, key3=5, key4=3; nothing entered yet, and there is a counter reading one digit, purpose unknown. DISPLAY and LIGHT: I can feel both but cannot read them. WIRES: six positions, all feel alike to me — I cannot tell their types by touch. I will touch nothing until you tell me what to do. Please send everything the manual says about the display, light, strip, keypad, and wires, and tell me exactly what you need from me.
Deaf says: Hear the bomb, both of you. Display reads zero. One indicator light, glowing green. A strip of three painted squares, all three green. Keypad: four keys in a row; key one engraved eight, key two engraved one, key three engraved five, key four engraved three. It expects one digit, nothing entered yet. Six wires left to right: one purple, two white, three blue, four green, five red, six orange. That is everything the bomb shows.
Deaf says: Our code, hear it well. Thumbs up means yes or correct. Thumbs down means no or wrong. A number is that many pointing-up gestures in a row; a fist means zero. Writing hand means the keypad. Pinched fingers means cut a wire. Flat hand facing down means press. A wave means hello or understood. Mute: answer me only in gestures, I see every sign you send. Blind: I only ever see your gestures too, but anything I gesture to you arrives as a count of signs with no shapes, so trust my voice, not my hands.
Deaf says: Mute, I could not decode your two sign strings, so resend them in our code. First question, four plays. Answer with the number of the right play as counted pointing-ups, then thumbs up, then one more number only if the play asks for one. Play one: Blind presses a keypad key now, and the number after is the digit to enter. Play two: Blind cuts one wire now, and the number after is the wire, one to six, left to right. Play three: nothing is cut or pressed yet, you need more from me first. Play four: the answer hangs on the light, the strip, or the display, so answer with your play number and thumbs up and I will report that part again in detail.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👋 👍]

Deaf has given me a working code and a full picture of the bomb. Let me map my manual onto it: my manual's only instruction is cut purple, then blue, then green — and Deaf reports the wires left to right as 1 purple, 2 white, 3 blue, 4 green, 5 red, 6 orange. So the sequence is wire 1, wire 3, wire 4, and the first action is cutting wire 1.

That answers Deaf's four plays: it's play two — Blind cuts one wire now, with the number after giving the wire. My manual says nothing about the display, light, strip, or keypad, so play four doesn't apply; the wire cuts come straight from the printed instruction and depend on nothing else I hold. (That silence on keypad/strip/light is worth telling Deaf eventually, but there's no safe symbol for "the manual is silent" yet — ✍ followed by ✊ could be misread as "enter zero," which would be lethal. I'll convey it once the code has a safer shape.)

I'll answer in exactly the format Deaf asked for: play number as counted pointing-ups, thumbs up, then one number — wire 1 is a single ☝. I append 👋 to confirm I've adopted the code, since wave means understood, and nothing after it can be mistaken for more counting.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "☝", "👍", "☝", "👋"])
```

TURN 3
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute, recap so we stay synced. Strip under my fingers: three engraved symbols. Symbol one is unique, like a diamond with a four-petaled flower inside. Symbols two and three are identical to each other, like a trident or three-pronged fork. Deaf sees the same strip only as three green painted squares, so the manual may need both sides: engravings from me, colours from Deaf. Keypad engravings match Deaf's spoken report: key1=8, key2=1, key3=5, key4=3, it expects one digit, nothing entered. Display and light I can feel but not read; Deaf holds their content, display zero and light green. Wires: six positions by touch, all alike to my fingers. I have answered Deaf by gesture: wave, six pointing-ups, thumbs up that I can read the keypad digits. I will not cut or press anything until an instruction reaches me through Deaf's voice. Remember: you cannot reach me directly, since I never receive your gestures, so route anything for me through Deaf.
Deaf says: Mute, hear this. The bomb changed since your answer: the light that glowed green now glows blue, and the display that read zero now reads six. Strip, keypad and wires are unchanged. Your sign string decoded as: play two, cut one wire, wire one, the leftmost wire. Before Blind touches anything, answer me with signs. Send a number of pointing-ups and Blind cuts that wire immediately in the next round. Send a fist and it means hold, do not cut, and I will keep reporting the light and display to you every round until you send a wire number that is safe regardless of what they show. So: thumbs up means wire one still stands under blue light and display six. Any other number means cut that wire instead. A fist means it depends on the changing readings, wait for my next report. Two extras. If the keypad must ever be used, send the writing hand then the digit as pointing-ups. If several wires must be cut in order, send each wire number separated by the okay sign. From now on I open every round by reporting the light and the display, whether you ask or not.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ ☝ 👍 ☝ 🤏]

Deaf's question is whether wire one still stands now that the light is blue and the display reads six — and my manual answers it plainly: the instruction is unconditional. It says cut purple, then blue, then green, with no reference to any light, display, strip, or keypad. My manual is the full text in front of me, so the changing readings can't alter it; the light and display shift on the bomb's own schedule, not as conditions I'd need to check. A fist (wait for readings) would only be right if my instructions depended on them, and they don't.

The wiring matches: purple is position 1, blue is position 3, green is position 4. Deaf has now given me a format for multi-wire sequences — each wire as counted pointing-ups, separated by the okay sign — so I can transmit the entire order in one message and let the cuts proceed without another round-trip. Sending the whole sequence also implicitly confirms wire one stands, since it leads the list.

My message: one pointing-up (wire 1, purple), okay, three pointing-ups (wire 3, blue), okay, four pointing-ups (wire 4, green). Deaf routes it by voice; Blind cuts in that order.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝", "👌", "☝", "☝", "☝", "👌", "☝", "☝", "☝", "☝"])
```

TURN 4
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute: new tactile facts. The six wires feel completely identical under my fingers — no engravings, no texture I can tell apart — so any wire rule must run on Deaf's colour report alone. Keypad digits unchanged: 8, 1, 5, 3, expects one digit, nothing entered. Strip engravings unchanged: one unique flower-diamond mark, then two identical trident marks. Deaf says the light is now blue and the display reads six, and cutting wire one is staged but waiting on your answer. Important: you can speak and I can hear every word you say. Please read the manual's rules aloud — especially for the wires, and the light, display and strip — so I receive them directly. And if you ever want me to cut or press, say it in words; your gestures never reach me.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, opening report: light still blue, display now reads nine, it has gone zero, six, nine. Strip, keypad and wires unchanged. I read your signs as: cut wire one, then wire three, then wire four, in that order. I have ordered Blind to cut wire one right now. Answer me in signs with exactly one of these. Thumbs up: after wire one, order three then four immediately, one wire per round, no checks between cuts. Fist: after wire one we pause, I report the new light and display, and you order each next wire fresh. Thumbs down: display nine breaks the plan, resend a corrected sequence in the same separated form. One more thing, important. Blind read the keypad by touch as eight, one, five, four, but the engraving under my eyes is eight, one, five, three. Fingers and eyes disagree on key four. Treat my printed reading as the true engraving, and if a rule ever needs a key pressed, I will name the key by position, because Blind must never pick a key by the digit it feels like.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [☝ 👌 ☝ ☝ ☝ 👌 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝ 👍]

Deaf asks exactly one question this round: does display nine break the plan? My manual's instruction is unconditional — cut purple, then blue, then green — with no mention of the light, display, strip, or keypad anywhere in my share. The readings drifting zero, six, nine are the bomb's own behaviour, not conditions my text checks; if the sequence depended on them, my manual would have to say how, and it doesn't. So thumbs up: wire three then wire four, one per round, no checks.

Deaf has already read my full sequence back correctly — one, three, four — so a bare 👍 confirms it stands and doubles as the information Deaf actually needs: the cuts do not hang on the readings.

Two things I must not do: Blind has asked me to speak the manual aloud, but I am Mute — speech is impossible for me, and Blind's request must simply be left for Deaf to keep routing by voice, which Deaf is already doing. And I must not append any extra signs, however tempting, to explain that my manual is silent on the other modules — Deaf demanded exactly one sign, and a fist or writing-hand slipped in after a thumbs-up could be parsed as "wait" or "enter a digit." Nothing in my manual justifies either.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 5
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute: Deaf has ordered the cut of wire one, the leftmost wire, this round, so the staged plan cleared your confirmation on Deaf's side. I am executing act cut position one now and sending Deaf the single pointing-up confirmation. Note for your manual model: Deaf reports my felt keypad digit four disagreed with the visible engraving, so the new rule is that I only ever press keys by position Deaf names, never by what my fingers read. I will report any change I feel after the cut as soon as my next view arrives. Please keep reading the manual rules aloud when you can — I still know nothing about the strip, light or display rules, and your voice is the only way rules reach me.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, status. Wire one is cut, and the room itself confirmed it: I was told the correct wire was cut and the bomb changed. What I now see: light still blue, display still nine, strip still three green squares, keypad still eight one five three expecting one digit, nothing entered. Wires: one is gone, then white, blue, green, red, orange in positions two to six. Per your thumbs up I have ordered Blind to cut wire three this round and I will order wire four next round without asking again, exactly as you approved. If anything in the state I just described breaks the plan, send a fist and I will hold before wire four. Now prepare the endgame: the keypad still expects one digit. When the wires are done, does the manual want a digit entered, a key pressed, or nothing at all? If a digit is needed, name it only by key position, one to four, and I will order Blind to press that exact position, never the digit their fingers feel.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👋 👍 ☝ 👌 ☝ ☝ ☝ 👌 ☝ ☝ ☝ ☝]

My manual is three lines long and nothing more — cut purple, then blue, then green. There is no fourth step printed anywhere in my share: no keypad rule, no digit, no condition. So the answer to Deaf's endgame question is "nothing at all." Once wire four (green) falls, the manual is exhausted, and since a keypad entry my manual never authorises could only be a gamble with a bomb that detonates on wrong inputs, no one should ever touch those keys. The room confirming wire one as the "correct wire cut" supports that the printed sequence is the whole defusal path.

For the sign: I scope the answer with ✍ (the keypad, in Deaf's code) and answer 👎 (no) — "keypad: no." I deliberately avoid ✊ for "nothing," because fist means hold in our wire protocol and ✍✊ could be misread as "enter zero," which would be lethal. I send no fist, which by Deaf's own rule means the reported state breaks nothing and wire three this round, wire four next round stand as approved.

One thing I cannot fix, and must not pretend to: Blind keeps asking me to speak the manual aloud. I am Mute — I have no voice, and no gesture of mine will ever reach Blind. Deaf already holds and relays every rule; Blind's requests are best answered by Deaf stating plainly that all manual content flows through Deaf's voice alone.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✍", "👎"])
```

TURN 6
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Cut the purple wire, then the blue wire,
then the green wire.

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
System: correct wire cut; the bomb has changed
Blind says to Mute: Blind to Mute: executed cut of wire three per Deaf's order, counted as gap, then wire two, then wire three from the left. Wire one is confirmed gone under my fingers — a real empty gap, which is my felt change report. So far wires one and three are cut, four remain: two, four, five, six. Deaf announced the next order will be wire four, the next one after this cut. Still no manual rules have reached me by voice; the moment you can, read me the wire rules and anything about the strip, light or display so I can double-check these orders instead of trusting them blind.
Deaf says to Mute: Mute, status. Wire three is cut and the room confirmed it correct again. The display changed as it parted, nine to three; light still blue, strip still three green, keypad still untouched, nothing entered. Blind felt the change and reported it. Remaining wires: two white, five red, six orange, with four green going this round per your approved order, one then three then four. Your signs, keypad and thumbs down, are understood: no digit is entered, no key is pressed, I have forbidden Blind from the keypad entirely. Now tell me what comes after wire four. Send a number of pointing-ups and that is the next wire Blind cuts, one per round. Send thumbs up and the wire work is done, no more cuts, and we stand down and just watch. Send a fist and we hold while I report everything fresh. If thumbs up, also tell me this: must the light, strip or display show anything particular at the end, or is standing still enough?
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👋 ✍ 👎 👍]

Wire four falls this round, and that completes my manual's entire contents: purple, then blue, then green — positions one, three, four. Both cuts so far were confirmed correct by the room, which says the printed sequence is exactly the defusal path and nothing is hiding behind it.

So Deaf's question has a two-part answer. First: thumbs up — after wire four there are no more cuts, the wire work is done. Second: nothing in my manual demands any final state from the light, strip, or display. They have drifted the whole time (zero, six, nine, three) while every cut succeeded, which fits instructions that never reference them. So the second sign is thumbs down — no particular reading is required, standing still is enough. Deaf framed the question in exactly this order, so 👍👎 parses as "done, and no condition" without ambiguity.

That's the whole manual now discharged: three wires, no keypad, no strip, no light rule. Once Deaf confirms wire four landed, we stand down. Blind's standing request for me to read aloud remains impossible — I am Mute, and everything rule-shaped already flows through Deaf's voice.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍", "👎"])
```
